questions.q: What does pip install --dry-run tell you?
options: What it would install, without installing it
questions.answer: What it would install, without installing it
questions.why: It looks at versions. It reads no code.

questions.q: What does a constraints file do?
options: It controls which version is installed, not whether one is
It installs every package listed in it
questions.answer: It controls which version is installed, not whether one is
questions.why: Pip's guide says that in almost those words.

questions.q: Why is a resolve failure on a dry run good news?
options: It happened on paper, and nothing in your environment moved
It means the pack is malicious
It means the pack has no requirements
questions.answer: It happened on paper, and nothing in your environment moved
questions.why: That is what you ran it for.

questions.q: What can a dry run not see?
options: A pack that calls pip from its own code at import
questions.answer: A pack that calls pip from its own code at import
questions.why: That's why you read the entry files first.

questions.q: Why mount models read-only in a sandbox?
options: A pack can't change weights it can't write to
It is the only way to use a GPU
questions.answer: A pack can't change weights it can't write to
questions.why: Containers help by what you don't give them.

questions.q: A graph breaks after you added several packs. What is the fastest way to find the culprit?
options: --disable-all-custom-nodes, then whitelist them one at a time
questions.answer: --disable-all-custom-nodes, then whitelist them one at a time

questions.q: A pack loaded fine in the sandbox. What have you shown?
options: That it loaded, and little more until its nodes have run
That it will work with every model
questions.answer: That it loaded, and little more until its nodes have run
questions.why: Hence the smoke test, and the rule that no layer is proof.
